inputs.root_cause: SAL-UBL-OBL-E98EB489DAC77A1A (UBL-EXT-001)'s 3-clause rule_text (expose media types, expose checksums, gate external retrieval) had media types already proven and external-retrieval gating correctly characterized as a structural absence (no fetch capability exists at all, same as UBL-SEC-001), but 'expose checksums' was genuinely unbuilt.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 3 new tests prove a new BinaryObject.checksum property returns the SHA-256 hex digest of the raw attachment bytes, differs for different content, and is independent of the declared mime_code (proving the payload is never decoded or interpreted, only hashed as opaque bytes).
inputs.regression_tier: full ubl package suite (tests/python/ubl) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Read the obligation's full rule_text: 'Treat extension payloads and embedded binary attachments as untrusted data; expose their media types and checksums without decoding side effects, and gate any external attachment retrieval behind allowlists, byte limits, and timeouts.' Confirmed 3 distinct clauses, only the second (checksums) genuinely unbuilt for BinaryObject.

2. Considered the 'extension payloads' half of the checksum clause too: no dedicated ExtensionContent model class exists in this package (extensions are preserved as raw XmlNode subtrees with no built-in byte-serialization helper), so building a checksum for arbitrary extension content would need a new serialization primitive -- deliberately scoped OUT of this slice as a separate, larger piece of work, not silently claimed.
3. Read BinaryObject's existing fields (values.py): already has .data: bytes directly available, making a checksum property trivial and low-risk to add.

4. Added BinaryObject.checksum, returning hashlib.sha256(self.data).hexdigest() -- hashing only the raw stored bytes, never the base64 wire form and never anything decoded from the declared mime_code, matching 'without decoding side effects' precisely.

5. Verified interactively before writing formal tests: checksum matches a manually-computed hashlib.sha256 digest, differs for different content, and is identical for the same bytes under different declared mime_code values (proving the payload itself, not its declared type, drives the hash) -- all correct on the first attempt.

6. Wrote 3 formal tests directly in the existing BinaryObject test section of test_obligation_business_value_types.py. Ran ruff (clean), the full ubl suite (779 passed, was 776, +3), and the full 6-format regression (3145 passed, was 3142, +3; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

7. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-f7afa8f69f7e14c6, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3145 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3142 passed

evidence.oracle: SELF-CONSISTENT format_factory-only evidence per the execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule.
